Package bakerydms

Class OrderValidator

  • java.lang.Object
    • bakerydms.OrderValidator
  • public class OrderValidator
extends java.lang.Object
    Keeps every data rule in one place and cleans up what the user types.

    Both OrderManager (before saving) and BakeryOrderWindow (to show hints and read typed values) use this class, so the program and the screen always apply the same rules. The orders table repeats the most important ones as CHECK constraints.

    The rules:

    • Order ID: 1000 to 9999, unique
    • Customer name: 2 to 30 letters, spaces, apostrophes, hyphens or periods
    • Phone number: exactly 10 digits, stored as 407-555-0142
    • Cake type: one the bakery sells (case is ignored)
    • Quantity: 1 to 50
    • Unit price: more than $0, at most $1000, 2 decimal places at most
    • Pickup date: a real date from today up to 2 years ahead
    • Special instructions: optional, up to 100 characters
    The parse... methods read typed text safely: they return an empty Optional instead of throwing an exception, so bad input can never crash the program.
    Version:
    4.0 (Phase 4, Module 11)
    Author:
    Kayla Ewing

      • formatPhone

        public java.util.Optional<java.lang.String> formatPhone​(java.lang.String rawPhone)
        Turns any reasonable phone number into the standard 407-555-0142 format. Spaces, dashes, dots, parentheses and a leading +1 are allowed in the input.

        Returns:
        the formatted number, or an empty Optional if it is not 10 digits

        public boolean isValidPrice​(double price)

      • parseDate

        public java.util.Optional<java.time.LocalDate> parseDate​(java.lang.String rawDate)
        Converts text into a date. Accepts YYYY-MM-DD (2027-02-13) or MM/DD/YYYY (2/13/2027). Impossible dates such as 2027-02-30 are rejected.
        Parameters:
        rawDate - the date as typed
        Returns:
        the date, or an empty Optional if the text is not a real date

      • parseWholeNumber

        public java.util.Optional<java.lang.Integer> parseWholeNumber​(java.lang.String text)
        Converts text to a whole number. Letters, decimals, blanks and numbers too large for an int are rejected instead of throwing an exception.
        Parameters:
        text - the text to convert, e.g. "1004"
        Returns:
        the number, or an empty Optional if the text is not a whole number

      • parseMoney

        public java.util.Optional<java.lang.Double> parseMoney​(java.lang.String text)
        Converts text such as "28", "28.50" or "$28.50" to a dollar amount. Words, negative numbers, "NaN", "Infinity" and "1e3" are rejected. (Whether the amount is allowed is checked separately by isValidPrice.)
        Parameters:
        text - the text to convert
        Returns:
        the amount, or an empty Optional if the text is not a plain dollar amount

      • normalize

        public Order normalize​(Order order)
        Returns a cleaned-up copy of an order: extra spaces removed, the phone number put in 407-555-0142 form and the cake type spelled correctly. Fields that are invalid are left as they are so validate() can report them.
